text.en: Look at your school bag. The bag is cloth, the zip is metal, the bottle is plastic and the pencil is wood. Why are different materials used for different things?

Everything around us is made of materials. An object can be made of one or many materials. Materials may come from nature, like wood and cotton, or be made by people, like plastic.
We group materials by their properties, such as hardness, shine, transparency, and whether they float or dissolve in water. Rough or smooth, hard or soft, light or heavy are also properties.
Metals are usually hard and shiny, and they conduct heat and electricity. Transparent materials like clear glass let light pass through completely. Translucent materials let some light through. Opaque materials, like wood and metal, let none through. Some solids dissolve in water, like salt and sugar, and some do not, like sand and chalk. Some materials float on water and some sink, depending on how heavy they are for their size.
Anything that has mass and takes up space is matter. Air is matter, even though we cannot see it, because it fills space and has weight. Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases.
We choose a material because its properties suit the use. Cooking pans are metal because metal conducts heat. Handles are plastic or wood because they do not conduct heat well.

problem.en: Why are windows made of glass?

text.en: So we can see through and let light in.

prompt.en: Explain why a pan has a plastic handle.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all shiny things are metal.

points.en: Transparent, translucent and opaque describe light passing.
Matter has mass and takes up space.
The choice of material depends on its use.
